title: Continuous Compatibility Lab
outcome: Continuously test modules against current and future interface versions
breakthrough: Ecosystem upgrades stop being surprise integration events

phases.name: Phase 1 - Build the Continuous Compatibility Lab Core

subphases.name: 1.1 Continuous Compatibility Lab Domain Model and State Plane
work: Define typed experiments, hypotheses, datasets, runs, and results required to continuously test modules against current and future interface versions, with explicit versions and validation at every boundary.

Implement an owned persistent state layer optimized for source code, tests, dependencies, architecture, performance, compatibility, and safe automated change; include snapshots or event history when state changes over time.
Expose create, query, update, subscribe, and delete operations through local APIs plus an SDK that never requires private cross-runtime imports.

subphases.name: 1.2 Continuous Compatibility Lab Execution Runtime
work: Build resumable workers and state machines that perform the core operation: continuously test modules against current and future interface versions.
Add cancellation, idempotency, bounded retries, timeouts, quotas, sandbox limits, and deterministic recovery from partial failure.
Create a local simulator that can replay success, malformed inputs, disconnection, overload, provider loss, and restart recovery.

phases.name: Phase 2 - Make Continuous Compatibility Lab Adaptive and Usable

subphases.name: 2.1 Continuous Compatibility Lab Decision and Learning Engine
work: Implement scoring, planning, prediction, search, or optimization using static analysis, dynamic tracing, program synthesis, mutation testing, and causal debugging.
Create feedback signals from task outcomes and user corrections; update tunable behavior without silently changing hard safety limits.
Return confidence, alternatives, bottlenecks, and a concise machine-readable explanation for every important automated choice.

subphases.name: 2.2 Continuous Compatibility Lab Interaction Surface
work: Build the primary experience in the code graph, repair workbench, live test arena, and architecture simulator, including live state, controls, errors, and recovery actions.
Add a CLI and typed client library so humans, agents, games, and third-party applications can operate the capability directly.
Stream progress and intermediate artifacts in real time so long operations remain inspectable, interruptible, and steerable.

phases.name: Phase 3 - Scale Continuous Compatibility Lab into a Breakthrough Product

subphases.name: 3.1 Continuous Compatibility Lab Offline, Edge, and Cloud Mesh
work: Implement local-only, hybrid, and cloud execution with explicit capability discovery and graceful behavior when optional peers disappear.
Add conflict-safe synchronization, workload placement, caching, backpressure, and failover across devices or nodes where the feature benefits from distribution.
Benchmark latency, throughput, memory, energy, network transfer, and cost; make the scheduler choose the best execution mode from measured constraints.

subphases.name: 3.2 Continuous Compatibility Lab Signature Breakthrough
work: Implement the differentiating behavior: Ecosystem upgrades stop being surprise integration events. Ship it as an opt-in executable mode, not a mockup.
Run adversarial, load, privacy, misuse, degraded-network, and recovery tests against the novel behavior; block unsafe automatic actions.
Package the feature as an independently installable capability with a live demo, sample integration, metrics endpoint, and rollback-safe release artifact.
